title: Hebrew names, and God’s care for the Christians
source_text: Καὶ οὕτω δὲ κατασκευαστέον ὅτι οὐκ Αἰγύπτιοι ἦσαν οἱ ἐξεληλυθότες μετὰ Μω(??)σέως τὴν Αἴγυπτον· εἰ μὲν Αἰγύπτιοι ἦσαν, ἐχρῆν αὐτῶν τὰ ὀνόματα εἶναι Αἰγύπτια, ὡς ἑκάστῃ διαλέκτῳ συγγενεῖς εἰσιν αἱ προσηγορίαι· εἰ δ᾿ ἐκ τῶν ὀνομάτων Ἑβραϊκῶν ὄντων σαφὲς ὅτι οὐκ Αἰγύπτιοι ἦσαν (πλήρης γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ τῶν Ἑβραϊκῶν ὀνομάτων καὶ τῶν ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ τοιαῦτα θεμένων τοῖς υἱοῖς), δῆλον ὅτι ψεῦδος τὸ λεγόμενον ὑπὸ τῶν Αἰγυπτίων. ὅτι Αἰγύπτιοι ὄντες ἀπηλάθησαν μετὰ Μωϋσέως ἀπὸ τῆς Αἰγύπτου· καὶ σαφῶς ἐναργές ἐστιν ὅτι ἐκ προγόνων Ἑβραίων κατὰ τὴν παρὰ Μωϋσεῖ ἀναγραφεῖσαν ἱστορίαν τὸ γένος ἔχοντες (ἰδίᾳ) διαλέκτῳ ἐχρῶντο, ἀφ᾿ ἧς καὶ τὰ ὀνόματα τοῖς υἱοῖς ἐτίθεντο. περὶ δὲ Χριστιανῶν, ἐπεὶ διδαχθέντες μὴ ἀμύνασθαι τοὺς πολεμίους ἐτήρησαν τὴν ἥμερον καὶ φιλάνθρωπον νομοθεσίαν, διὰ τοῦθ᾿ ὅπερ οὐκ ἂν ἐξουσίαν λαβόντες τοῦ πολεμεῖν, εἰ καὶ πάνυ ἦσαν δυνατοὶ, ἤνυσαν· τοῦτ᾿ ἀπὸ θεοῦ εἰλήφασι, τοῦ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν πολεμήσαντος ἀεὶ καὶ κατὰ καιροὺς παύσαντος τοὺς κατὰ Χριστιανῶν ἱσταμένους καὶ ἀναιρεῖν αὐτοὺς θέλοντας. ὑπομνήσεως μὲν γὰρ χάριν, ἵνα ἐνορῶντες ὀλίγοις ἀγωνιζομένοις ὑπὲρ εὐσεβείας δοκιμώτεροι γίνωνται καὶ θανάτου καταφρονῶσιν, ὀλίγοι κατὰ καιροὺς καὶ σφόδρα εὐαρίθμητοι ὑπὲρ τῆς Χριστιανῶν θεοσεβείας τεθνήκασι, κωλύοντος θεοῦ τὸ πᾶν ἐκπολεμηθῆναι αὐτῶν ἔθνος· συστῆναι γὰρ αὐτὸ ἐβούλετο καὶ πληρωθῆναι πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν τῆς σωτηρίου ταύτης καὶ εὐσεβεστάτης διδασκαλίας· πάλιν τε αὖ ἵν᾿ οἱ ἀσθενέστεροι ἀναπνέωσιν ἀπὸ τῆς περὶ τοῦ θανάτου φροντίδος, ὁ θεὸς προὐνοεῖτο τῶν πιστευόντων, μόνῳ τῷ βουλήματι διασκεδαννὺς πᾶσαν τὴν κατ᾿ αὐτῶν ἐπιβουλὴν, ἵνα μήτε βασιλεῖς μήτε οἱ κατὰ τόπους ἡγούμενοι μήτε οἱ δῆμοι ἐξαφθῆναι κατ᾿ αὐτῶν ἐπὶ πλεῖον δυνηθῶσι, ταῦτα μὲν πρὸς τὰ ὑπὸ Κέλσου εἰρημένα περὶ τοῦ στάσιν γεγονέναι τὴν ἀρχὴν πάλαι μὲν τοῦ συστῆναι Ἰουδαίους ὕστερον δὲ τοῦ τοὺς Χριστιανοὺς γενέσθαι.
pass_a_gloss: And thus it must be established (κατασκευαστέον) that those who came out of Egypt with Moses were not Egyptians: if they were Egyptians, their names (ὄνομα) ought to be Egyptian, as to each language the appellations (προσηγορία) are akin (συγγενής); but if from the names being Hebrew it is clear that they were not Egyptians (for the Scripture (γραφή) is full of Hebrew names and of those in Egypt who gave (τίθημι) such to their sons), it is plain that the thing said by the Egyptians is a lie, that being Egyptians they were driven out (ἀπελαύνω) with Moses from Egypt; and it is clearly evident (ἐναργής) that, having their race from Hebrew forefathers (πρόγονοι) according to the history (ἱστορία) recorded (ἀναγράφω) by Moses, they used (their own) language, from which they also gave names to their sons. But about Christians: since, taught not to defend themselves against enemies, they kept (τηρέω) the gentle (ἥμερος) and humane (φιλάνθρωπος) legislation (νομοθεσία), for this reason what they would not have achieved (ἀνύω) having received authority (ἐξουσία) to make war (πολεμέω), even if they were very powerful (δυνατός), this they have received from God, who has always fought for them and at times (κατὰ καιρούς) stopped (παύω) those rising (ἵστημι) against Christians and wishing to kill them. For for the sake of reminder (ὑπόμνησις), so that looking upon (ἐνοράω) a few contending (ἀγωνίζομαι) for piety (εὐσέβεια) they may become more approved (δοκιμώτεροι) and despise death (θάνατος), few at times and very easily counted (εὐαρίθμητος) have died for the worship of God (θεοσέβεια) of Christians, God hindering (κωλύω) their whole nation (ἔθνος) from being warred out (ἐκπολεμέω); for he wished (βούλομαι) it to stand (συνίστημι) and the whole earth to be filled (πληρόω) with this saving (σωτήριος) and most pious (εὐσεβέστατος) teaching (διδασκαλία); and again, so that the weaker (ἀσθενέστερος) might take breath (ἀναπνέω) from the anxiety (φροντίς) about death, God provided (προνοέω) for those believing, by his will (βούλημα) alone scattering (διασκεδάννυμι) every plot (ἐπιβουλή) against them, so that neither kings nor the governors (ἡγούμενοι) in [various] places nor the populaces (δῆμοι) could be kindled (ἐξάπτω) against them further. These things [are said] against what was said by Celsus about revolt having been the beginning long ago of the Jews’ forming (συνίστημι) and later of the Christians’ coming to be.
pass_b_english: That those who left Egypt with Moses were not Egyptians may also be argued in this way. If they had been Egyptians, their names ought to have been Egyptian, since in every language the names belong to that language. But if it is clear from their names, which are Hebrew, that they were not Egyptians (for Scripture is full of Hebrew names, and of people in Egypt who gave such names to their sons), then the Egyptians’ claim that they were Egyptians driven out of Egypt with Moses is plainly false. And it is quite evident that, being descended from Hebrew ancestors according to the history recorded by Moses, they used their own language, from which they also named their sons.

As for the Christians: because they were taught not to defend themselves against their enemies, and kept the gentle and humane legislation, they have received from God what they would not have accomplished had they been given leave to make war, even if they had been very powerful: from God, who has always fought for them, and from time to time has stopped those who rose up against the Christians and wished to kill them.

For as a reminder, so that by looking upon a few contending for godliness they might be of more proven worth and despise death, a few at various times, and very easily counted, have died for the Christian worship of God, while God prevented their whole nation from being wiped out by war. For he willed that it should be established, and that the whole earth should be filled with this saving and most godly teaching. And again, so that the weaker might have respite from their anxiety about death, God provided for those who believe, scattering every plot against them by his will alone, so that neither kings nor local governors nor the populace could be inflamed against them any further.
So much in answer to what Celsus said: that revolt was the beginning, long ago, of the Jews’ coming together as a people, and later of the Christians’ coming into being.

choices.choice: Copy-text: staged source_3.json section 8 (Koetschau 3.8). The staged text has a damaged first ‘Μω(??)σέως’; read as Μωϋσέως (Moses), as the name is spelled later in the same row. ‘(ἰδίᾳ)’ is an editorial supplement and is translated (‘their own language’). ‘πλήρης γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ τῶν Ἑβραϊκῶν ὀνομάτων καὶ τῶν ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ τοιαῦτα θεμένων τοῖς υἱοῖς’: taken as ‘full of Hebrew names, and of people in Egypt who gave such names to their sons’, keeping the two genitives that depend on πλήρης (the genealogies of Exodus 1:1–5 and 6:14–25 would be examples; not cited inline because Origen points to no passage). ‘τοῦ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν πολεμήσαντος’ may echo Exodus 14:14 (‘the Lord will fight for you’); possible allusion only, not cited inline. ‘πληρωθῆναι πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν τῆς … διδασκαλίας’ may echo Isaiah 11:9 or Habakkuk 2:14 (the earth filled with the knowledge of the Lord); possible only, not cited inline. ‘δοκιμώτεροι’ rendered ‘of more proven worth’ (more tested and approved). ‘θεοσέβεια’ rendered ‘worship of God’; ‘εὐσέβεια’ ‘godliness’. ‘ἐκπολεμηθῆναι’ rendered ‘wiped out by war’. ‘συστῆναι’ rendered ‘be established’. ‘ἀναπνέωσιν ἀπό’ rendered ‘have respite from’. ‘οἱ δῆμοι’ rendered ‘the populace’. The relative clause ‘τοῦ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν πολεμήσαντος …’ stays attached to God (‘from God, who has always fought for them’) rather than becoming a new ‘For’ sentence; ‘ἀναιρεῖν’ rendered ‘kill’. No LXX renumbering arises.

wrong sense: the parenthesis said Scripture’s Hebrew names ‘include those which people in Egypt gave their sons’; the Greek says Scripture is full of Hebrew names and of people in Egypt who gave such names to their sons
‘plainly what the Egyptians say is false, that they …’ reordered to ‘the Egyptians’ claim that … is plainly false’
added ‘For God has always fought for them’ made the relative clause it is in the Greek (‘from God, who has always fought for them’); ‘destroy’ made ‘kill’ (ἀναιρεῖν)
omitted γάρ restored (‘For as a reminder’); ‘more steadfast’ made ‘of more proven worth’ (δοκιμώτεροι)
‘breathe freely from anxiety’ made ‘have respite from their anxiety’ (ἀναπνέωσιν ἀπό)
